## Purpose

This pull request removes support for prefills from the 3D kernel and its corresponding reduce kernel.

The 3D and reduce kernels implement parallel tiled softmax computation, which is particularly advantageous in scenarios with small batch sizes and long sequences (i.e., long KV contexts). In such cases, these kernels enable increased parallelism, allowing for more effective utilization of GPU resources.

Prefill operations, however, typically involve many query tokens which inherently provide sufficient parallelism. In these cases, the 2D kernel is better suited for efficient processing, rendering the 3D kernel support for prefills unnecessary.

By removing this redundant support, the kernel logic is simplified without compromising performance.

This is a **tiny** perf improvement (5us per MLA layer), meaning a total of ~55us per forward. With ~13ms per forward this means it's not quite measurable within the noise from vllm bench serve. title: [Spec Decode] Add cuLA KVBuffer backend for Lightning Attention
body: ## Motivation This PR adds an optional cuLA KVBuffer backend for Lightning Attention in Ling-2.6-flash speculative decoding. Linear-attention serving is IO-sensitive: the recurrent decode path reads and writes a large per-request state on every token, and speculative verification can require temporary state for each draft token. The KVBuffer paper ([arXiv:2605.19049](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.19049), "KVBuffer: IO-aware Serving for Linear Attention") describes a serving design that buffers recent K/V and verifies speculative draft tokens in parallel, then commits only the accepted prefix into the linear-attention state. In particular, Figure 2 in the paper illustrates the speculative-decoding pattern targeted here: buffer draft K/V, compute verification outputs from the initial state plus buffered K/V, and update the state once after acceptance.
